query: Say It So It Lands Seraphine stops halfway through a sentence and looks at the candle across the observatory. "That will go out," she says, quite clearly, "when I've finished the next word." It does. "Saying it is the spell. Seeing it is just… I can teach you the saying part." Learn to say it out loud It takes the whole night, and it's unsettling to hear your own voice go flat and certain. Near dawn you foretell a dropped spoon and the spoon drops. Seraphine smiles at something next week. Ask what she sees for you "Quiet," she says. "Yours is always quiet." She doesn't teach you tonight. She says you'll ask again, and you know she's right, which is the strange part.
